headline: Precompute palindrome ranges, then choose every valid next piece
statement: Return every partition of s into contiguous nonempty substrings such that each piece is a palindrome. The pieces in each partition must concatenate to s. Return partitions in any order.
intuition: At an offset, any palindromic prefix of the remaining suffix may be the next piece. A palindrome table makes every proposed cut a constant-time lookup instead of repeatedly scanning its interior.
approach: Fill palindrome[left][right] for increasing substring lengths using equal endpoints and the inner range.
Search from start; try every end whose table entry is true.
Append that substring, recurse at end+1, and undo the choice.
Record path when start reaches the string length.
correctness: The table recurrence is exact: a range is palindromic iff endpoints match and its interior is palindromic, with length one or two handled directly. Each partition has a unique sequence of cut positions. The search tries every next palindromic range and only such ranges, so it enumerates every valid partition exactly once.
bruteForce: Try all 2^(n-1) cut masks and independently scan each resulting substring for symmetry.

complexity.explanation: The table costs n². In the worst case every cut pattern is valid, and copying pieces across outputs costs O(n×2^n).

pitfalls: A partition covers the full string without skips.
Do not confuse this with finding one longest palindromic substring.
